body_html:
Honda Vietnam and Yamaha Motor Vietnam publish scooter service figures in different forms: Honda in a mileage table (read here in one owner manual, the LEAD 125) plus FAQ entries, Yamaha in free-service voucher windows and web articles. This article reads those pages for the scooter service interval each states, using pages dated between September 2021 and September 2026, and flags where they disagree. None of the pages mentions rental bikes, and the section "What the pages leave out" lists what is missing.

How Honda publishes its schedule

Honda's service page defines periodic inspection as servicing at a set cycle, given by distance or time, and says Honda Vietnam researched and recommends the frequency and content to suit riding conditions in Vietnam. The page has separate schedule tabs for bikes above 350cc, below 350cc and electric bikes. The tables themselves did not come through in the extracted text. The page adds that at higher odometer readings the schedule repeats.

The LEAD 125 owner's manual, copyright 2024, shows the layout: columns at 1, 6, 12, 18, 24, 30 and 36 thousand km, with a note that beyond the last column the cycle repeats. Notes beneath the table say maintenance should be more frequent when riding in wet or dusty conditions, in rain or at high speed, and that replacements need repair skills. The table lists final-drive oil and brake fluid at 2 years and radiator coolant at 3 years. Which service item falls in which mileage column could not be read, so the manual's engine-oil interval is not available here. The manual also says maintenance is the responsibility of the user and that periodic service counts as the owner's running cost, paid to the authorised Honda store. For finding a manual for a particular bike, see Find the Exact Manual for Your Rental Scooter: Model Code, Year and Market.

What Honda's FAQ and warranty page say

Honda's FAQ, in entries updated on 20 and 21 September 2021, says oil-change timing for motorbikes (the entry's term is xe gắn máy) depends on the bike's condition, how much it is used, speed, load, environment and oil grade, so it advises following the manual's schedule. In ordinary conditions, it says, oil must be changed after the first 1,000 km and should then be changed every 6,000 km, with a shorter interval for use above 1,000 km a month. It puts final-drive oil at about 2 years, shorter with heavy loads or long-distance riding, and says coolant should be checked every 15,000 km or 12 months and replaced after 30,000 km or 36 months. During the warranty, it adds, an engine-oil change at an authorised store is charged at the store's price, because Honda does not provide free replacement of the oils on the Table 2 in the warranty booklet.

Honda's warranty page, which applies from 15 August 2025 until Honda changes it, gives bikes of 350cc or less 36 months or 30,000 km, whichever comes first, when the warranty is activated within 7 days of purchase, and 35, 34 or 33 months if activated later. It lists customer obligations: follow the manual, do periodic checks on schedule and replace parts and fluids as the manual says. Otherwise, the page says, Honda refuses warranty repair. Wear parts, oils and similar items are excluded, with engine oil on the list.

How Yamaha structures service visits

Yamaha's 20 September 2026 article says a new scooter not yet in frequent use should be serviced every 2 to 3 months or by mileage. It says new Yamaha bikes come with nine free service vouchers covering 3 years or 30,000 km, in three levels: one level-1, five level-2 and three level-3. Each voucher has a window in months after purchase.

VoucherWindow after purchase
1Within the first 4 months
2Months 5 to 10
3Months 11 to 14
4Months 15 to 18
5Months 19 to 22
6Months 23 to 26
7Months 27 to 30
8Months 31 to 34
9Months 35 to 38

Yamaha's periodic-maintenance page says that using the first three vouchers fully and on time at an authorised dealer extends the warranty by 1 year or 10,000 km, to 2 years or 20,000 km, whichever comes first. Using vouchers 4 to 6 as well extends it again, to 3 years or 30,000 km, for bikes under 400cc.

Yamaha's oil and parts figures

The same 20 September 2026 article gives part-by-part figures for scooters.

ItemFigure in the article
Engine oilEvery 1,500 to 2,000 km, sooner depending on use
Gear (final-drive) oilEvery 6,000 to 8,000 km
CoolantAdd coolant after 10,000 km
Spark plugReplace after 10,000 km
Drive beltMaintain every 3,000 km, replace after 25,000 km
Air filterCheck and replace before 16,000 km
Brake padsReplace at 15,000 to 20,000 km
TyresCheck and replace every 15,000 to 20,000 km
BatteryCheck the electrolyte concentration monthly

For reading the manufacturer's tyre-pressure label, see Motorbike Tyre Pressure for Rental Riders: Read the Manufacturer Label.

Where the pages disagree

SourceEngine oilGear or final-drive oil
Yamaha article, 20 September 2026Every 1,500 to 2,000 kmEvery 6,000 to 8,000 km
Yamaha article, 24 September 2026First change at 500 to 1,000 km, then every 2,000 km (new bike) or 1,000 to 1,500 km (older bike)Every third engine-oil change, about 5,000 to 8,000 km
Yamaha scooter oil page, undatedAfter the first 500 to 1,000 km, then every 1,000 to 1,500 kmAbout 5,000 to 6,000 km, or every third engine-oil change
Honda FAQ, 21 September 2021After the first 1,000 km, then every 6,000 km in ordinary conditionsAbout 2 years
Honda LEAD 125 manualNot readable in the extract2 years

The 24 September article's engine-oil figures are for motorbikes in general (xe máy); only its gear-oil figure is given for scooters. Two figures also sit uneasily with their own pages: the last Yamaha voucher window runs to month 38 although the warranty figure is 3 years, and the 24 September article's "every third engine-oil change, about 5,000 to 8,000 km" does not match its own per-change figures (three changes of 1,000 to 2,000 km come to 3,000 to 6,000 km).

The Yamaha pages differ with one another and with Honda's FAQ, which gives a longer engine-oil interval, and none explains why. The 24 September article says timing is not fixed and varies with bike type, riding habits and age; the undated service page says it varies with the oil used, speed, load and operating conditions. The 24 September article, which cites experts and service centres, also gives a general price range of 80,000 to 500,000 VND or more for an oil change, depending on bike type, oil and location. It gives no dealer price.

Wet, dusty and heavy use

Honda's pages agree on one point: conditions can bring service forward. The manual and warranty page call for more frequent maintenance in wet or dusty conditions or at high speed, and the FAQ advises checking and servicing at shorter intervals than the standard schedule in the rainy season. After flooding, the FAQ says to check the engine oil, and on a scooter the final-drive oil too, and to change the engine oil before starting if water got in. For a floodwater scenario written for rental riders, see A Rental Scooter Caught in Floodwater: Stop, Record and Contact the Shop.

What the pages leave out

No page mentions rental bikes, so what a rental shop services, when, and who bears the cost is not covered. Honda's manual speaks of the user and the owner, and its FAQ says an oil change during the warranty is paid at the store's price, without addressing hired bikes. Honda's schedule tables were not readable, so no Honda oil interval here comes from a manual. The Honda FAQ entries used here date from September 2021 and are not tied to a model, and Yamaha's figures come from web articles and service pages rather than an owner manual. Two Yamaha pages and the Honda service page are undated. The Honda warranty page lists, among excluded uses, commercial use as a public-transport vehicle; it does not mention rental bikes. The vouchers apply to new Yamaha bikes, and no page says how they work for any other bike. No page gives a Honda service price or a Yamaha dealer price.

Sources checked

  • Honda Vietnam: Periodic maintenance page
  • Honda Vietnam, applies from 15 August 2025: Warranty policy page
  • Honda Vietnam: LEAD 125 owner manual
  • Honda Vietnam, entries from September 2021: FAQ page
  • Yamaha Motor Vietnam, 20 September 2026: Scooter maintenance article
  • Yamaha Motor Vietnam, 24 September 2026: Oil change article
  • Yamaha Motor Vietnam, undated: Scooter oil service page
  • Yamaha Motor Vietnam, undated: Periodic maintenance and warranty page

Thuê xe máy Nguyễn Hà is open 09:00–21:00 daily at Ngõ 5 Nguyễn Văn Cừ, Bồ Đề, Long Biên, Hà Nội (near Gia Lâm bus station). Phone: 0334 699 969.
